newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: UN begins food handouts in Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: UN begins food handouts in Sierra Leone.

text.p: The United Nations World Food Programme said on Friday it had begun distributing food in Sierra Leone because stocks of essentials had dwindled since the military coup on May 25.
The food, from existing stocks that had mostly escaped looting after the coup, will be distributed in Freetown and other urban centres.

The WFP was already helping feed people in hospitals, schools and orphanages there, but it said in a statement issued by its regional office in Ivory Coast that thousands more had arrived in the towns in need of help.
The WFP said the price of staple foods had doubled since the coup, and supplies of imports such as rice, sugar and flour had fallen.
"Kerosene and petrol are also in short supply, and it is expected that many essential products such as fuel and rice will run out within two weeks," it added.
